messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: control-plane error spike detected. 5xx + timeouts across gateway -> auth, org-lookup, billing. Alert window 18:22 UTC. Paging oncall @tj.

oncall-tj: I'm on it. grabbing top-line metrics now — 5xx rate ~28% across requests to /v1/*, error surge began ~18:17 UTC. Gateway 502/504s increasing.

alex: seeing org-lookup latency ramping — p50 60ms -> p95 3.2s, p99 ~9s. Auth upstream returning 504s intermittently. Billing calls showing 502s from config service.

maya: any customer-impact summary? are write paths failing or read-only degraded?

oncall-tj: most user-facing failures are in auth flows (login/token exchanges) and any API that needs org metadata. Some embeddings calls succeed but chat flows that require org validation get 5xx. Estimate: ~12% of active requests currently failing user-visible.

trent: running quick health checks. curl to control-plane gateway:
```
$ curl -i https://api.redwood.dev/health
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Server: envoy
date: Mon, 03 Mar 2025 18:25:10 GMT

```

emily: k8s events for org-lookup service show repeated liveness probes failing on one node:
```
E042 18:19:33.123 kubelet healthcheck failed for pod org-lookup-5f8d7
OOMKill: process killed due to memory spike
```

alex: interesting — but auth 504s aren't all from org-lookup. We have an upstream token-service rate-window limit kicking in -> returning 429 then gateway mapping to 504/502. Could be circuit interactions.

oncall-tj: immediate mitigations proposed: (1) enable org-lookup cached fallback for 30m (serve stale org metadata) via feature-flag; (2) temporarily raise token-service rate limit for control-plane clients; (3) scale org-lookup deployment + restart pods on failing node; (4) enable gateway retry/backoff reduction.

maya: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/control-plane-deps.json — follow "orglookup / auth cascade" section. I'm going to flip cache-fallback now.

oncall-tj: agree. Maya, can you put the cache-fallback flag in /featureflags control-plane? I can handle scaling + pod restarts.

maya: flipping flag:
```
POST https://config.redwood.internal/featureflags
{ "key": "orglookup_stale_fallback", "value": "on", "ttl": 1800 }
```

maya: flag applied. Confirmed via logs: "orglookup fallback enabled, serving stale for key=org-1234"

trent: scaling org-lookup from 3 -> 9 replicas now (HPA manual override).
```
kubectl scale deploy org-lookup --replicas=9 -n control-plane
```

ops-bot: action log: org-lookup replicas scaled to 9 by trent at 18:29 UTC.

emily: restarted the failing pod; new pod shows steady memory under 600Mi.

alex: token-service rate-limit temporarily raised for control-plane-clientID=cp-core to 10k/min. watch for abuse.

oncall-tj: monitoring — 5xx now dropping: 28% -> 11% in 6 minutes. Gateway 502s reduced. Auth 504s still occasional but trending down.

maya: starting limited canary rollback for latest org-lookup image (there was a recent change to caching that could be memory heavy). Rolling back canary to previous stable on 20% of traffic.

trent: added circuit-breaker on billing->config path to fast-fail after 3s to reduce head-of-line blocking.

alex: quick note for customer comms: affected requests were mainly login/org metadata requests. If asked, tell customers we've mitigated with cached fallback and autoscaling; full root cause investigation ongoing.

oncall-tj: handing off to maya for overnight watch and RCA. I'm going offline in 20. @maya please take oncall ownership.

maya: taking handoff. I'll keep the dashboard pinned and escalate if 5xx >10% for 15m. I'll create RCA ticket and link logs. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident runbook updated: incident-2835016420 (heartbeat-throttle-chain) created. Pager duty cleared to note: mitigations applied, oncall handoff to maya.

oncall-tj: final note — temporary flags & rate-limit increases are in place; we need a follow-up: optimize org-lookup memory usage, add stronger backpressure on token service, and add better cached stale-serving logic to avoid full failure.

maya: acknowledged. I'm kicking off RCA ticket now and will post update in this thread in ~2hrs with logs and root cause hypothesis.

emily: leaving a small traceback snippet for the RCA: "panic: map allocation failed" in org-lookup cache loader when concurrent loads hit pathological keyset.

maria (bot): reminder: post-incident checklist: run alert debrief, rotate temporary keys, schedule follow-up meeting.

maya: thanks team, closing active mitigation. continuing watch. :wave:
